## TL;DR

Human-assigned tasks now share a single `humanTaskGuideWarning()` that nudges authors when `## Step-by-step guide` is missing, still scaffold-only, or contains bullets without numbered steps. Warnings surface on CLI create/update/split, HTTP task APIs, and in the task drawer for open human work. PM and engineer default prompts, split-human-step canned text, scaffolds, and split templates were updated so agents file actionable guides. Review feedback drove fence-aware section parsing, drawer status guards, split API warnings, consolidated placeholder constants, and tests including `--section "Step-by-step guide"`.

## Work and rationale

The motivating failure was practical: held human tasks (keystore backup, provider signup, on-device checks) often shipped as two-line acceptance criteria, forcing the human to reverse-engineer steps afterward. AI tasks already had a strict body contract; human tasks are the one place the reader cannot infer missing detail, yet nothing asked for it.

The fix is deliberately soft—warnings, not errors—so legacy human tasks keep working while new and updated tasks get immediate feedback. Centralizing validation in `src/core/task-underspecified.ts` keeps CLI (`src/commands/tasks.ts`), HTTP (`src/server/routes/tasks.ts`), and the Vue drawer (`TaskDrawer.vue`) aligned, matching how underspecified and needs-human-step checks work elsewhere.

Guide quality checks require at least one numbered step (`1. …`), not bullets alone, matching the spec. Placeholder italic text from `HUMAN_SPLIT_GUIDE_PLACEHOLDER` in `human-step-tags.ts` is treated as unfilled so an empty scaffold cannot pass silently. The human task scaffold and `buildHumanTaskBody` for splits both import that constant.

Fenced-code awareness mattered because sample task bodies can show a `## Step-by-step guide` heading inside a markdown code block; naive line scans would treat that as a real section and suppress warnings. A shared `isMarkdownFenceClose()` in `src/core/markdown-fence.ts` implements CommonMark-style closing (bare fence characters only), used by guide extraction and engineering-report summary validation in `task-summary.ts`.

The drawer banner hides for `done` and archived tasks so completed legacy human work is not nagged. Split actions return a `warning` field on the HTTP response and log on the CLI when the spawned human task still has a placeholder guide.

Documentation stays thin in `AGENTS.md` (one line plus link) with detail in `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md` and `user-docs/cli.md`, including the “still empty” message for placeholder-only or bullet-only guides.

## Approaches tried

Initial implementation wired warnings only for missing headings; review caught scaffold-only guides passing validation. The filled check was extended to strip placeholder lines and require `^\d+\.\s` substantive content.

Fence handling started with `trimmedStart.startsWith(fence)`, which incorrectly closed blocks on info-string openers like ` ```md `. Extracting a small helper and mirroring it in both guide parsing and summary validation fixed the class in one change.

Review round 4 flagged foreign `work/*.md` bookkeeping on the branch; those paths were dropped (main’s copy wins) and main was merged again on this resume turn so landing preflight stays clean.

## Challenges and blockers

A prior turn ended with a network error before handoff, leaving the task active with review fixes largely implemented but not re-verified. Merging main after that pause picked up unrelated task bookkeeping on the branch tip only; the code diff stayed scoped.

Declaring a UI shot for the drawer banner proved brittle in automated capture (fixture timing); behavior is covered by unit tests, `drawer:humanGuideWarning` preview fixture, and an earlier successful capture noted in review evidence.

Remote validation in `repoos check` adds wall-clock time but exercises the same changed-path suite reviewers care about.

## Key learnings

Human-task ergonomics benefit from the same “warn early at the write surface” pattern as AI underspec checks, but with different content rules (actionable steps, secrets handling, success criteria) and no `needs_input` flag. Sharing one function across CLI, API, and UI avoids drift.

Markdown task bodies need fence-aware section parsing anywhere headings gate product behavior; a one-line `startsWith` fence close is a recurring footgun worth a shared helper and table-driven tests.

Placeholder text in scaffolds must participate in “empty” detection using the same constant the template renders, or template edits can silently weaken enforcement.
